newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Endemol shares slide as results disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Endemol shares slide as results disappoint.

text.p: Shares in Endemol Entertainment NV, one of Europe's biggest television production companies, tumbled in Amsterdam on Tuesday as the company's first set of post-flotation results disappointed the market.

Endemol, floated on the Dutch bourse last November, reported that net profit for the first half of the 1996/97 financial year ended January 31 rose 19 percent to 33.7 million guilders from 28.3 million a year earlier.
But this fell short of analysts' forecasts of 36 to 40 million guilders and the company's shares closed four guilders or 6.6 percent lower at 57.00.

Endemol said the acquisition of the Holiday on Ice skating spectacle company had helped to boost first-half turnover by 38 percent to 441 million guilders but that the new unit's profits had not matched up to its expectations.
"The net result of Holiday on Ice is disappointing due to declining demand for live entertainment, particularly in the German and French markets," the company said.
By contrast Endemol said its Dutch stage production of the Miss Saigon musical, which opened half way through the reporting period, had proved a big box office success so far.
Endemol said its core television production business, good for 75 percent of group turnover, had not been harmed by the collapse of the short-lived Sport 7 channel.

Co-chairmen Joop van den Ende and John de Mol had borne the direct losses while the newly formed Endemol Sports unit had been able to produce programmes for other broadcasters which had acquired the rights previously held by Sport 7.

Analyst Patrick Wollenberg of Rabo Securities noted that the increase in Endemol's profits was only half as big as the increase in turnover and said it was interesting that the company admitted Holiday on Ice had performed disappointingly. "This clearly confirms our view that Endemol's expansion beyond television production in the Netherlands is accompanied by higher risks," he said.
Wollenberg said he had lowered his rating for Endemol to a Sell in December and that he was sticking to this. "We think the fall in the share price today is fully justified," he said.
